quests.instruction: Snap the scrambled words back into the order you hear.
quests.hint: Two subordinate ideas stack before the main clause even begins: a reason, and a time frame inside it.
quests.explanation: 'Because' + reason (the server crashed) + 'while' + time clause (we were deploying) + main clause (the release was delayed). A time clause can sit nested inside a reason clause.
quests.textToSpeak: Because the server crashed while we were deploying, the release was delayed.

quests.instruction: Listen closely, then rebuild the sentence in the order you hear it.
quests.hint: 'By the time' marks a deadline inside the reason clause, before the main action follows.
quests.explanation: 'Since' + reason ('she'd already left by the time I called', containing its own time clause) + main clause (I emailed instead). A reason clause can contain a full time clause of its own.
quests.textToSpeak: Since she'd already left by the time I called, I emailed instead.

quests.instruction: Put the scrambled words back in the order you hear them.
quests.hint: A contrast clause opens, and a time clause closes — the main idea sits between the two.
quests.explanation: 'Although' + contrast (he'd prepared thoroughly) + main clause (he still felt nervous) + 'once' + time clause (the interview began). Contrast and time clauses can frame a main clause from both sides.
quests.textToSpeak: Although he'd prepared thoroughly, he still felt nervous once the interview began.

quests.instruction: Snap the scrambled words back into the order you hear.
quests.hint: 'Had already calmed down' shows the main event finished before the time clause's event even happened.
quests.explanation: 'By the time' + time clause (the ambulance arrived) + main clause (the situation had already calmed down, past perfect). Past perfect shows the main event was complete before the time clause occurred.
quests.textToSpeak: By the time the ambulance arrived, the situation had already calmed down.

quests.instruction: Listen closely, then rebuild the sentence in the order you hear it.
quests.hint: 'Once' plus present tense refers to a future trigger point, similar to 'when'.
quests.explanation: 'Once' + condition (the contract is signed, present) + result (we can start ordering materials). 'Once' shows the result follows immediately after the condition is met.
quests.textToSpeak: Once the contract is signed, we can start ordering materials.

quests.instruction: Put the scrambled words back in the order you hear them.
quests.hint: 'As soon as' signals immediacy — the result follows right after the condition, without delay.
quests.explanation: 'As soon as' + condition (the results are confirmed, present) + result ('we'll notify everyone involved'). 'As soon as' emphasizes that the second action happens without any gap.
quests.textToSpeak: As soon as the results are confirmed, we'll notify everyone involved.

quests.instruction: Snap the scrambled words back into the order you hear.
quests.hint: The whole subject, participle phrase included, comes before the passive verb 'was sent'.
quests.explanation: Subject (A detailed report outlining the budget shortfall, adjective + participle phrase) + 'was sent' + 'to every department head'. The participle phrase adds detail without a full relative clause.
quests.textToSpeak: A detailed report outlining the budget shortfall was sent to every department head.

quests.instruction: Listen closely, then rebuild the sentence in the order you hear it.
quests.hint: Two participle-style modifiers stack: one before the noun, one after it.
quests.explanation: Subject (The newly appointed director overseeing the merger, past participle + present participle phrase) + verb (starts) + time ('on Monday'). Both a past and present participle can modify the same noun.
quests.textToSpeak: The newly appointed director overseeing the merger starts on Monday.

quests.instruction: Put the scrambled words back in the order you hear them.
quests.hint: 'Carefully worded' and 'addressing the complaint' both describe the email, from two different angles.
quests.explanation: Subject (A carefully worded email addressing the complaint, adverb + participle + participle phrase) + verb phrase (went out) + time ('this afternoon'). Multiple modifiers can layer onto one noun without becoming a full clause.
quests.textToSpeak: A carefully worded email addressing the complaint went out this afternoon.

quests.instruction: Snap the scrambled words back into the order you hear.
quests.hint: 'Having reviewed' opens the sentence, showing that action happened before the main one.
quests.explanation: 'Having' + past participle (reviewed) + object (the data) + main clause (the analysts recommended a different approach). 'Having' plus a past participle shows the opening action finished before the main clause.
quests.textToSpeak: Having reviewed the data, the analysts recommended a different approach.

quests.instruction: Listen closely, then rebuild the sentence in the order you hear it.
quests.hint: This time the opening participle is present tense, still showing the cause behind the main action.
quests.explanation: 'Realizing' + object (the mistake too late) + main clause (she sent a follow-up apology). A present participle opener can explain the reason behind the main clause.
quests.textToSpeak: Realizing the mistake too late, she sent a follow-up apology.

quests.instruction: Put the scrambled words back in the order you hear them.
quests.hint: 'Faced with' is a passive-style participle opener, showing a situation the team found themselves in.
quests.explanation: 'Faced with' + situation (limited options) + main clause (the team decided to postpone the launch). Passive participle openers like 'faced with' describe a circumstance affecting the subject.
quests.textToSpeak: Faced with limited options, the team decided to postpone the launch.

quests.instruction: Snap the scrambled words back into the order you hear.
quests.hint: 'Currently' shows the review is an ongoing process happening right now.
quests.explanation: Subject (The committee) + 'is currently reviewing' + object (applications) + 'for the fellowship'. 'Currently' with present continuous is common in formal status updates.
quests.textToSpeak: The committee is currently reviewing applications for the fellowship.

quests.instruction: Listen closely, then rebuild the sentence in the order you hear it.
quests.hint: 'Ensure that' introduces a formal instruction, followed by a passive embedded clause.
quests.explanation: 'Please ensure that' + embedded clause (all invoices are submitted, passive) + deadline ('by the end of the quarter'). 'Ensure that' is a common formal way to give an instruction in writing.
quests.textToSpeak: Please ensure that all invoices are submitted by the end of the quarter.

quests.instruction: Put the scrambled words back in the order you hear them.
quests.hint: 'Suggest' softens the claim slightly, common in careful academic language.
quests.explanation: Subject (The findings) + verb (suggest) + object (a strong correlation) + 'between the two variables'. 'Suggest' is used in academic writing to present evidence carefully, without overclaiming.
quests.textToSpeak: The findings suggest a strong correlation between the two variables.

quests.instruction: Snap the scrambled words back into the order you hear.
quests.hint: 'Before proposing' shows the correct order: diagnosis has to come first.
quests.explanation: Subject (We) + 'need to' + verb (identify) + object (the root cause) + 'before' + gerund (proposing a solution). 'Before' plus an '-ing' form shows which step must happen first.
quests.textToSpeak: We need to identify the root cause before proposing a solution.

quests.instruction: Listen closely, then rebuild the sentence in the order you hear it.
quests.hint: The condition names the problem, and 'should' offers advice based on that condition.
quests.explanation: 'If' + condition (the current approach isn't working) + advice (we should reconsider our strategy). This conditional structure frames practical advice around an observed problem.
quests.textToSpeak: If the current approach isn't working, we should reconsider our strategy.

quests.instruction: Put the scrambled words back in the order you hear them.
quests.hint: 'Narrowed down to' is a phrasal expression meaning 'reduced to one specific answer'.
quests.explanation: Subject (The team) + phrasal verb (narrowed down) + object (the issue) + 'to a single faulty component'. 'Narrow down to' describes the process of eliminating options until one remains.
quests.textToSpeak: The team narrowed the issue down to a single faulty component.

quests.instruction: Snap the scrambled words back into the order you hear.
quests.hint: 'Rarely' at the front flips the normal order — the auxiliary jumps ahead of the subject.
quests.explanation: 'Rarely' + 'have' + subject (I) + past participle (seen) + object ('such a thorough analysis'). Starting with a negative adverb like 'rarely' triggers subject-auxiliary inversion for emphasis.
quests.textToSpeak: Rarely have I seen such a thorough analysis.

quests.instruction: Listen closely, then rebuild the sentence in the order you hear it.
quests.hint: 'Not only' at the start forces the same kind of inversion, with 'did' appearing before the subject.
quests.explanation: 'Not only' + 'did' + subject (the project) + base verb (succeed) + 'but' + clause 2 (it also came in under budget). 'Not only...but also' emphasizes two positive facts together, with inversion in the first clause.
quests.textToSpeak: Not only did the project succeed, but it also came in under budget.

quests.instruction: Put the scrambled words back in the order you hear them.
quests.hint: 'Only after' also triggers inversion — 'did we' instead of the usual 'we did'.
quests.explanation: 'Only after' + condition (reviewing every option) + 'did' + subject (we) + base verb (make) + object (our final decision). 'Only after' at the start of a sentence also causes inversion in the main clause.
quests.textToSpeak: Only after reviewing every option did we make our final decision.

quests.instruction: Snap the scrambled words back into the order you hear.
quests.hint: 'Which' here refers back to the entire first event, not just one word in it.
quests.explanation: Main clause (The client rejected the proposal) + ', which came as a shock to the team'. 'Which' can refer back to a whole preceding idea, not just a single noun.
quests.textToSpeak: The client rejected the proposal, which came as a shock to the team.

quests.instruction: Listen closely, then rebuild the sentence in the order you hear it.
quests.hint: 'Something' stands in for the entire situation just described, not one specific object.
quests.explanation: Main clause (He missed the deadline again) + ', something his manager wouldn't overlook'. 'Something' can summarize a whole preceding action as a single reference point.
quests.textToSpeak: He missed the deadline again, something his manager wouldn't overlook.

quests.instruction: Put the scrambled words back in the order you hear them.
quests.hint: 'A trend' relabels the entire previous event as a single noun, which 'that' then describes further.
quests.explanation: Main clause (Costs rose sharply last quarter) + ', a trend that concerns the board'. This structure renames a whole event as a noun before adding a relative clause about it.
quests.textToSpeak: Costs rose sharply last quarter, a trend that concerns the board.

quests.instruction: Snap the scrambled words back into the order you hear.
quests.hint: The whole opening clause acts as the subject, delaying the real point until after 'is that'.
quests.explanation: Subject ('What the data seems to suggest', a whole clause) + verb (is) + 'that' + embedded clause (customer loyalty is declining). This structure builds anticipation before revealing the actual finding.
quests.textToSpeak: What the data seems to suggest is that customer loyalty is declining.

quests.instruction: Listen closely, then rebuild the sentence in the order you hear it.
quests.hint: 'As far as I can tell' is a softening phrase inserted right in the middle of the sentence.
quests.explanation: Subject (The main challenge) + inserted phrase (', as far as I can tell,') + verb (is) + object (a lack of clear communication). Inserted softening phrases can interrupt a sentence without breaking its structure.
quests.textToSpeak: The main challenge, as far as I can tell, is a lack of clear communication.

quests.instruction: Put the scrambled words back in the order you hear them.
quests.hint: 'Whatever the outcome' dismisses uncertainty upfront, before the main opinion follows.
quests.explanation: 'Whatever the outcome' + main clause (the team deserves credit for their effort). 'Whatever' plus a noun shows the following statement holds true regardless of that variable.
quests.textToSpeak: Whatever the outcome, the team deserves credit for their effort.

quests.instruction: Snap the scrambled words back into the order you hear.
quests.hint: A participle opener, a relative clause, and a nested time clause all combine in one long, natural sentence.
quests.explanation: 'Having identified the root cause' (participle opener) + main clause (the engineers proposed a fix) + relative clause ('that, once implemented, should prevent future failures', containing a nested time clause). Multiple B2 structures nest inside one another here.
quests.textToSpeak: Having identified the root cause, the engineers proposed a fix that, once implemented, should prevent future failures.

quests.instruction: Listen closely, then rebuild the sentence in the order you hear it.
quests.hint: A contrast clause opens, and a participle phrase interrupts the main clause before it finishes.
quests.explanation: 'Although' + contrast (the findings were inconclusive) + subject (the committee) + inserted participle phrase (', faced with a looming deadline,') + verb (approved) + object (the proposal) + 'anyway'. An inserted participle phrase can interrupt a main clause for extra context.
quests.textToSpeak: Although the findings were inconclusive, the committee, faced with a looming deadline, approved the proposal anyway.

quests.instruction: Put the scrambled words back in the order you hear them.
quests.hint: A time clause, a relative clause, and a past perfect result all combine to show a slightly ironic outcome.
quests.explanation: 'By the time' + time clause (the report was finalized) + main clause ('the very issue it addressed had already resolved itself', containing an omitted-pronoun relative clause). Past perfect shows the resolution happened before the report was even complete.
quests.textToSpeak: By the time the report was finalized, the very issue it addressed had already resolved itself.
